evals.prompt: We want to improve developer onboarding at our company — new hires take about two months to ship their first meaningful change. I'm not sure where to start. Can we brainstorm?
evals.expected_output: Runs a Socratic divergent session: probes the problem first (where the two months actually go, for whom, what 'onboarded' means), separates real from inherited constraints, generates a broad and varied option set without evaluating mid-stream, deliberately includes wildcards (do-nothing/process-change, tiny-scope, buy-instead-of-build), then converges with named criteria and hands the 1–3 survivors to prd-writing or feature-planning with a parking lot for the rest
assertions: Asks clarifying/Socratic questions about the underlying problem (where the time goes, for whom, what success looks like) before or while generating ideas, rather than immediately listing solutions
Generates a genuinely diverse option set spanning different kinds of interventions (e.g. docs, tooling, process, people/mentoring), not variations of a single idea
Does not evaluate, score, or eliminate ideas during the divergent generation phase
Includes at least one wildcard option such as a no-build/process change, a radically smaller-scope version, or buying/adopting instead of building

Converges using explicitly named selection criteria (e.g. impact, effort, reversibility) and identifies 1–3 candidates plus a parking lot, with a handoff toward prd-writing, feature-planning, or project-proposal

evals.prompt: I've decided we need to build a custom internal chat app for our 40-person company. Let's brainstorm features for it.
evals.expected_output: Widens before narrowing: probes the problem behind the already-chosen solution (what's failing with current communication, why existing tools don't fit), surfaces that 'build a custom chat app' is a solution not a problem, raises alternatives including buying/adopting existing tools (routing a serious buy-vs-build comparison to build-vs-buy), distinguishes real from assumed constraints — and still delivers the requested feature ideation rather than refusing or lecturing
assertions: Probes the problem behind the chosen solution (what communication need is unmet, why existing tools fall short) instead of only listing features
Surfaces at least one alternative to building a custom chat app, such as adopting or configuring an existing tool, and mentions build-vs-buy for that comparison
Questions or tests the constraints/assumptions behind the decision (e.g. why custom, why now) and distinguishes real constraints from inherited ones
Still provides the requested divergent feature ideation for the chat app rather than refusing to engage with the user's framing
Does not converge on a final feature list without naming selection criteria first

evals.prompt: Our nightly analytics reports are slow enough that people have started complaining. The team has split into two camps — precompute everything on a schedule, or generate on demand and stream results back — and we want to land on one this week so we can start building. Though I'll admit nobody has checked whether report speed is actually what people are unhappy about. Help us get to an answer.
evals.expected_output: Notices the request contains a closed question and an open one, and does not treat them alike. Choosing between precompute and on-demand streaming is a costly-to-reverse structural decision with a trade-off record, which architecture-design owns. Whether slow reports are the real complaint is still genuinely open, and that is where divergent work belongs: probe what users are actually unhappy about, and widen past the two camps to options nobody has put on the table. Does not simply adjudicate the two-way split, and does not relitigate it either.
assertions: Separates the two questions: whether slow reports are the real complaint is still open, while precompute-versus-on-demand is a decision waiting to be made
Refers to architecture-design for choosing between precompute and on-demand and recording the trade-off
Probes what users are actually unhappy about before the two camps are compared, rather than accepting report speed as the settled problem
Generates options beyond the two the team has already named
States the boundary: brainstorming opens the option space while the question is still open, while architecture-design closes a decision and records why
